newsitem.title: USA: UroQuest seeks FDA approval for catheter.
newsitem.headline: UroQuest seeks FDA approval for catheter.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has advised UroQuest Medical Corp it must adopt a different method to get approval for one of its catheters before it can market it, the company said Wednesday.
UroQuest said it had received a letter from the administration clarifying its policy on transurethral occlusive devices for the management of lower urinary tract dysfunction.
"The FDA ...indicates that all such devices should now be regulated through the premarket approval process," it said.
"Although no specific products were identified in the FDA's communication, this broad definition appears to encompass UroQuest's Male and Female On-Command(R) Catheters."

The company said it had been pursuing a 510(k) regulatory path for the Male On-Command Catheter based in part on a prior communication from the FDA. The 510(k) is generally a shorter regulatory path than the one being advocated by the administration, it said.
UroQuest said it planned to meet with the FDA in mid-February to discuss the matter.
The company designs, develops and manufactures products for the management and diagnosis of urological disorders.
